title: An Efficient Checkpointing System for Large Machine Learning Model Training
problem: Checkpointing large ML models with trillions of parameters is extremely time and storage consuming, creating a bottleneck in training. Writing massive models to checkpoints frequently incurs prohibitive storage and I/O performance overhead.
motivation: Efficient checkpointing is critical for fault tolerance in large-scale ML training, but I/O costs become prohibitive as models scale to trillions of parameters.
method: The system proposes periodic cleanup of outdated checkpoints to reduce storage burden, and data staging optimization that coordinates checkpoint movement between local and shared file systems for improved I/O performance. Evaluation is performed on GPT-2 variants.
key_novelty: Combining periodic checkpoint cleanup with data staging between local and shared filesystems to simultaneously address storage and I/O performance bottlenecks in large model training.
contributions: Characterization of checkpointing overhead in large ML/language models for storage and performance
Periodic cleaning strategy to reduce storage burden from accumulated checkpoints
Data staging optimization coordinating I/O between local and shared file systems
2.1× performance improvement and constant storage reduction for GPT-2 training
primary_theme: Efficient checkpointing for large ML model training
